# This hangar

`CLAUDE.md` beside this file says how a hangar works and is the same in every one. This file says
which hangar this is, and every value in it comes from `hangar.config.yaml`.

| | |
| -------------------- | --- |
| hangar root          | %HANGAR% |
| hangar id            | vsfix |
| repo                 | git@bitbucket.org:example/storefront_ui.git |
| default branch       | release |
| clone directories    | `checkout_<NN>`, at least 4 digits — e.g. `checkout_0001` |
| app subdirectory     | `web/` |
| secrets              | `%HANGAR%/.env.vsfix-shared` (mode 400) |
| shared plans         | `%HANGAR%/plans` |
| shared tmp           | `%HANGAR%/tmp` |
| issue keys           | `UI-…`, `PLAT-…` |

**Which clones exist is in no file, this one included.** They are whatever `checkout_<NN>`
directories are there; index gaps are normal, because `hangar remove-clone` never renumbers —
renumbering would move another clone's ports out from under a running server. `hangar list` is
the only answer, and `git -C checkout_0001 branch --show-current` the only answer about a branch.

## Ports

Every clone's ports are a pure function of its index:

    port = base + 0 + (index - 1) * 50

| role | env var | base | URL |
| ---- | ------- | ---- | --- |
| Next dev server | `VSFIX_WEB_PORT` | 4200 | `https://local.example.invalid:{port}/app` |
| Storybook | `VSFIX_STORYBOOK_PORT` | 6006 | `http://localhost:{port}` |
| Playwright report | `VSFIX_E2E_REPORT_PORT` | 9323 | `http://localhost:{port}` |

The offset is this hangar's residue class mod 50, and that is the whole
guarantee: two hangars with different offsets can never collide for any clone counts, unlike a
reserved block, which fails silently once a hangar outgrows it. **Never hard-code a port and never
assume a server on a default port is yours** — `hangar ports` is the answer for the fleet, and
each clone's own `CLAUDE.local.md` names its own.

## Symlinks every clone carries

Targets are shown AS DECLARED: `{secretsFile}`, `{index2}` and the rest are rendered per clone.

- `web/e2e/.env.local` → `{secretsFile}` — the Playwright project reads web/e2e/.env.local and the tracked web/e2e/.env sets the password empty AFTER direnv, so this reload is what wins
- `web/.env.secrets` → `{secretsFile}` — the Next.js dev server reads .env.secrets from the app directory and will not look above it, so the shared file has to appear inside web/

## Per-clone variables beyond the ports

In every clone's `.env.development.local`, rendered from its index:

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME={displayName} {index}`
- `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME={id}_{index2}`
- `REDIS_NAMESPACE={clone}`
